notes: Gujarat's 2026-27 counselling has begun: PIN purchase and online registration from 01/10/2026 to 08/10/2026, and document checks at a Help Centre from 03/10/2026 to 09/10/2026. The registration, eligibility and registration-fee lines here are from the 2026-27 papers. Gujarat hasn't published its 2026-27 round rules yet, so the round cards are its 2025-26 rules, tagged as such.

In 2025-26 Gujarat's Admission Committee counselled government, management and NRI seats together in four online rounds: Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 (earlier the mop-up) and Round 4 (the final stray vacancy round). We hold no 2025-26 prospectus; the round rules are a Gujarati notice, the 2020 bond orders are Gujarati too, and the lines from them are our English.

r1.title: Round 1
chips: Free exit for all, deposit kept
who: 2026-27: buy the registration PIN online (Rs 3,000 non-refundable plus a Rs 25,000 refundable security deposit, Rs 28,000 in all) by 08/10/2026 03:00 PM, and register and upload your documents by 08/10/2026 05:00 PM. Then take your documents to the Help Centre slot you booked (03/10/2026 to 09/10/2026): without that check and the stamped registration slip you can't go further.

Eligibility for 2026-27: an MBBS from a university in Gujarat; or an MBBS from elsewhere in India or abroad (meeting NMC's criteria) with Class 12 in the B or AB group from a school in Gujarat, and born in Gujarat or domiciled there. Internship must be complete by 30/09/2026.

In-service candidates: citing a Government resolution of 10/01/2022, the registration procedure gives them 10% of all PG seats in ten MD/MS subjects (Paediatrics, TB and Chest, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Preventive and Community Medicine, Orthopaedics, General Surgery, General Medicine, Anaesthesiology, Radiology, Pathology) in the government quota of government and GMERS colleges, and in government-quota CPS courses at government hospitals. They need an NOC from Gujarat's competent authority.
Disability (PwD) quota: you're examined by the Admission Committee's own Medical Board, and only its certificate counts; no other disability certificate is accepted.

NRI seats: merit is by all-India overall NEET-PG rank among the NRI applicants. NRI candidates are verified only at the Committee's office at GMERS Medical College, Gandhinagar, with notarised copies, and also give a Rs 25,000 non-refundable processing draft.
After the merit list, choice filling opens online for each round.
opts: Pay the allotted college's tuition fee, deposit your originals at the Help Centre, report, and collect the admission order. In every round you pay one term (six months) of tuition and show the receipt; for an NRI seat the term fee is Rs 10 lakh by demand draft. NRI candidates, those with an MBBS from outside Gujarat or India, and in-service and other special-category candidates get their appointment only at GMERS Medical College, Gandhinagar.

Whether you got no seat, didn't report, or reported, you can take part in Round 2 on your old registration, with free exit and without losing the deposit.
gaps: how the free exit works for a candidate who reported: the notice says only that such candidates can take part in Round 2 (the cancellation window is under Round 2).
r1.yearnote: Who can take part is from Gujarat's 2026-27 papers. What you can do after an allotment is its 2025-26 rules: its 2026-27 round rules aren't out yet.

r2.title: Round 2
who: Round 1 registrants who verified their documents needn't register again; others register fresh (Rs 28,000 PIN) and verify documents.
ins: p.1; a60: p.2
opts: You give up your confirmed Round 1 seat. If you then don't confirm the new seat, both rules apply: you have no claim on the Round 1 seat, and not confirming a Round 2 allotment forfeits the deposit.
Your Round 1 admission stays, with nothing more to do.
Pay the fee, deposit your originals and take the admission order; you can then take part in Round 3.
The refundable deposit is forfeited. To enter Round 3 you register again, with a new PIN fee and a new deposit.
Cancel a confirmed Round 1 or 2 admission

In 2025-26 the Help Centre took cancellations of Round 1 and 2 admissions from 01/01/2026 to 05/01/2026 04:00 PM. Go in person (or a parent, with an authority letter) with an application to cancel, the original admission order, a copy of the fee receipt, a self-attested copy of any all-India, deemed, central or other-state allotment letter (or, if not admitted anywhere, the cancellation application) and ID, and collect your originals. Fees are refunded after the admission process if you take no admission; no penalty or forfeiture is stated. An older copy of this paper adds that fees are adjusted if you take a Round 3 seat and that the same seat stays open to you; the 2025-26 copy leaves both out.

The candidates, who have confirmed their admission after submitting the original documents at the Help Center, want to cancel the admission, they will have to go to the admission reported Help Center, in-person.
gaps: which fees are refunded on a cancelled admission (tuition, PIN fee or deposit): the cancellation paper doesn't say.
r2.yearnote: These are Gujarat's 2025-26 rules: its 2026-27 round rules aren't out yet.

r3.title: Round 3 (earlier the mop-up)
chips: Give online consent to take part
After this round: final, no later round
who: Give online consent, or you aren't considered. Earlier registrants who verified their documents and got no Round 2 seat needn't register again; new candidates, those who qualified under the revised cut-off, and those whose deposit was forfeited register (Rs 28,000 PIN). You can change your Round 1 and 2 choices.

Once every reserved-category candidate on the merit list has been admitted, unfilled reserved seats go to the unreserved category in this round; NRI seats can convert to management seats, and management seats to government quota. Each conversion happens only when eligible candidates of that category are exhausted.
amd: p.1
opts: Your Round 1 or 2 admission is cancelled automatically; report at the same Help Centre for the new admission order.

If the candidates, who have confirmed the admission of 1st round/2nd round and have given consent to participate in 3rd Online MOP UP round, have been allotted any new different seat (upgradation of admission), the admission of the 1st round/2nd round will get automatically cancelled.

You keep your Round 1 or 2 seat, must study there, and can't take part in any later State or all-India round. The Gujarati notice adds that a seat confirmed in Round 2 and not upgraded in Round 3 can't be cancelled in any circumstances.

If the candidates, who have confirmed the admission of 1st round/2nd round and have given consent to participate in 3rd Online MOP UP round, have not been allotted any new different seat, the admission of the 1st round/2nd round will be continued.
Category or quota change in the same college

Whether or not you took part in Round 3, your earlier admission can be moved up in the same college by a change of category (ST, SC, SEBC or EWS to general, or PwD to non-PwD) or of quota (government to institutional); you needn't report to the Help Centre for it.
The candidate, who have participated or not participated in 3rd Online MOP UP Round, the admission of previous round can also be up-graded in the same college by change of admission category
Pay the tuition (or the difference) and report for the admission order. The seat is final: no later State or all-India round, and it won't be cancelled in any circumstances.

If candidate is allotted a seat, Candidate has to take print of allotment order of 3rd Online MOP UP round, pay the tuition fees/difference of tuition fees if any and report to the help center to get your admission order.
The new admission is cancelled and you're left with no seat (an upgraded candidate has lost the earlier one too); the deposit is forfeited and you're out of later rounds.
In case you don’t report to help center within stipulated time your new admission is treated cancelled.
gaps: whether the English paper's 'must study there' and all-India bar, written for candidates who give Round 3 consent, also bind a Round 1 or 2 seat-holder who gives none. The Gujarati notice bars every candidate still holding a confirmed seat at the end of Round 3 from Round 4, consent or not, and says a Round 2 seat not upgraded in Round 3 can't be cancelled.
the time limit for reporting after a Round 3 allotment: the process paper says only 'within stipulated time'.
r3.yearnote: These are Gujarat's 2025-26 rules: its 2026-27 round rules aren't out yet.

stray.title: Round 4 (final stray vacancy)
chips: Only if you confirmed no seat
who: New registration is open (Rs 28,000 PIN). The Gujarati notice admits candidates who confirmed no seat in State Rounds 1 to 3 and weren't allotted in Round 3; the Round 4 advertisement names only those who never registered, and Round 2 allottees who didn't confirm and didn't register for Round 3.
Not eligible: anyone allotted a seat in Round 3, and anyone who confirmed a seat in Rounds 1 to 3 of all-India or State counselling and still held it when Round 3 ended.

after.title: Leaving the course
chips: Service bond: Rs 2 lakh to Rs 40 lakh (2020 orders)
opts: The 2025-26 documents state no rupee penalty for leaving a seat. But a confirmed Round 3 seat, or a seat confirmed in Round 2 and not upgraded in Round 3, can't be cancelled in any circumstances, the Gujarati notice says. The 2018 admission rules, which may say more, aren't among the documents we hold.

Government-college seats (not all-India quota) carry a Rs 40 lakh bond, given to the Dean at admission, for at least one year of rural service after the course (365 working days, public holidays included; other leave extends it), backed by a Rs 10 lakh bank or property guarantee valid 7 years and a Rs 30 lakh undertaking. The order is from 2020, says it's subject to a pending High Court appeal, and isn't restated for 2025-26.
Service bond, GMERS and self-financed colleges (2020 order)

The 2020 order for these colleges is titled for SC and ST students who get a free-ship card: they give the same Rs 40 lakh bond for one year of rural service. It says other GMERS students, who pay the Fee Committee's fee, give a bond of Rs 2 lakh, or the amount GMERS fixes, for one year's service where the Government posts them. It doesn't mention full-fee students at other self-financed colleges. This order is also subject to the pending High Court appeal.
gaps: whether the 2020 bond orders still apply in 2025-26.
whether full-fee students at self-financed colleges outside GMERS give any service bond: the 2020 order doesn't say.
after.yearnote: These are the 2025-26 papers and the 2020 bond orders: Gujarat's 2026-27 papers so far don't cover leaving a seat or the bond.

reg: 2026-27: PIN Rs 3,000, non-refundable, the same as 2025-26. A lost PIN costs Rs 500 to regenerate, at GMERS Medical College, Gandhinagar; keep it until the refund process is over. NRI candidates also pay a Rs 25,000 non-refundable processing draft. In 2025-26, re-registering after losing the deposit meant buying a new PIN.
dep: 2026-27: Rs 25,000 refundable security deposit, paid with the PIN (Rs 28,000 in all). No category-wise or government-versus-private split is stated.
lose: 2025-26 rules (2026-27's aren't out yet): a Round 2 or Round 3 allotment you don't confirm (fee unpaid, originals not deposited). Round 4: not stated.
back: 2025-26 papers: when the deposit is refunded isn't stated. Fees on a cancelled admission are refunded after the admission process if you take no admission; which fees isn't stated.
leave: No penalty stated for 2025-26. 2020 bond orders: Rs 40 lakh for one year of rural service at government colleges (not all-India quota) and for SC and ST free-ship students at GMERS and self-financed colleges; other GMERS students Rs 2 lakh.
